findings.title: Error from deferred a.Close() is ignored
findings.message: The deferred app.Close() return value is discarded, so teardown failures of the app (window/process release, final flushes) are silently dropped in every run of this test.
findings.suggestion: Surface the Close error in the test so resource teardown problems are reported:

findings.title: t.Fatalf inside the validation loop hides subsequent contract failures
findings.message: The page/modal contract loop uses t.Fatalf on the first validation failure, so only one broken page or modal combination is reported per run. When a change breaks several views at once (e.g. a shared widget refactor), each run surfaces only the first violation and the rest require repeated fix cycles.
findings.suggestion: Use t.Errorf instead of t.Fatalf so the loop continues and every failing page/modal combination is reported in a single run:

findings.title: Service payload tests only cover the happy path
findings.message: Every Validate call in this test passes a well-formed payload, so a Validate implementation that unconditionally returns nil (or that has a broken condition) would pass all assertions. The negative paths of the Notification, TrayOptions, and FileOptions contracts are never exercised.
findings.suggestion: Add table-driven negative cases asserting that invalid payloads are rejected, e.g. app.Notification{ID: ""}, app.TrayOptions{Title: ""}, and app.FileOptions{Mode: app.SaveFile, Extensions: nil} each return a non-nil error from Validate.
